organism.overview: Androctonus australis is a medically important scorpion that delivers venom through its sting. Human risk varies with species, dose, route, and individual susceptibility.
naturalHistory: It is adapted to arid and semi-arid environments.
Scorpions use pincers and a venomous telson during predation and defense.
Activity and encounters vary with temperature and habitat conditions.

deliveryMechanism.summary: Venom is delivered through the stinger at the end of the tail.
sequence: Scorpion restrains or contacts a target.
Venom is injected through the sting.

habitats.name: Arid and semi-arid landscapes
habitats.summary: Associated with dry environments in North Africa and adjacent regions.

ecologicalRoles.summary: Venom contributes to prey immobilization and defense.

summaryPoints: Scorpion envenoming is a medically recognized exposure pathway.
